# How to allow text commands to be modified during robot motion rather than pre-generating entire trajectories?

> **Current answer:** TextOp uses the current text and recent robot motion to generate short motion blocks on G1, which are executed by an independent 50 Hz tracker, allowing text to be updated without interrupting the controller; the paper reports input to visible response at ~0.73 seconds and 30-second real machine trial denominators, but the system does not perceive the environment and cannot treat open text as safe and executable commands.

## Credibility and review status

- **Handbook level:** `L3 Reviewed engineering conclusion`
- **Level note:** This conclusion has passed the Handbook EngineeringClaim review gate.
- **Confidence:** `0.77`
- **Confidence rationale:** Real 30-second trials have explicit denominators and latency measurements, offline representation/tracker ablations are extensive, and official code maps the streaming mechanism. Confidence is capped by small real samples, environment blindness and repository version caveats.
- **Safety level:** `caution`

## Result

- TextOp uses the current text and recent robot motion to generate short motion blocks on G1, which are executed by an independent 50 Hz tracker, allowing text to be updated without interrupting the controller; the paper reports input to visible response at ~0.73 seconds and 30-second real machine trial denominators, but the system does not perceive the environment and cannot treat open text as safe and executable commands.

## Limitations

- Commands fall near the BABEL/text training vocabulary and describe kinematically supported behaviors.
- An external workstation and a robust G1 motion tracker are available.
